**Describe the bug**
We are trying to run multiple clips with alpamayo 1.5 in one session. 
We can process a single clip without a crash, but as soon as we want to process multiple clips in a batch the session crashes for all clips except the first with CUDA errors (see below).

comments.body: Hey, thanks you for reporting! I'll push a new container version soon (the NuRec team just released an updated version) and will ping you here, hopefully that fixes that.

Thanks for the quick reply,

looking forward, testing it.

Can you try following command to repro the issue? I don't see the CUDA error with it.

uv run alpasim_wizard +deploy=local wizard.log_dir=$PWD/muti_scenes scenes.scene_ids=['clipgt-02eadd92-02f1-46d8-86fe-a9e338fed0b6','clipgt-a309e228-26e1-423e-a44c-cb00aa7378cb','clipgt-804afc4a-fd1e-4f58-bd39-a4c486a916e5','clipgt-81b0e06d-96e6-4832-99c1-a4084b54ca97','clipgt-9b3509c2-a5fa-42c0-b0e5-feb617e9bf4e','clipgt-90d1908c-9fdc-40ea-a5a1-351240aa323e','clipgt-7c4f23b7-be14-4505-b332-6d1ceb36cd75']

Hi @daehyoungko 
Thanks for suggestion. I already tried it this way. In fact I tried this before moving the clips into the deployment config file.
My workaround is to start the alpasim_wizard in a script that loop through the clips in data/scenes/sim_suites.csv and start each clip separately. So after each clip, the containers are restarted. This works so far.

I wonder if it is possible, that the GPU memory is not sufficient (4  * 3080 GPUs with 10 GB each) for NuRec? Is there a way to configure alpasim to utilize two GPUs for one NuRec session? Can NuRec make use of more than one GPU?
The option  `gpuss [0,1]` in the `sensorsim` section of  the deployment config just seems to increase the number of sensorsim containers instead of assigning both GPUs to one container.

Good point about the memory. I'd assume the error to look different, but maybe?
Quick question: You say you have four GPUs, but in the config you shared, you're only using the first one? 
For reducing the memory footprint of NuRec, try setting `defines.nre_cache_size` to 1 or 2.

> Good point about the memory. I'd assume the error to look different, but maybe? Quick question: You say you have four GPUs, but in the config you shared, you're only using the first one? For reducing the memory footprint of NuRec, try setting `defines.nre_cache_size` to 1 or 2.

Sorry for the confusion. I already changed the GPU config to make use of different GPUs per microservice. My current config looks like this:
``` yaml
services:
  # No driver service needed - it's external

  sensorsim:
    replicas_per_container: 1 # Number of service replicas per container
    gpus: [1,2] # GPUs to create containers on     

  physics:
    replicas_per_container: 1
    gpus: [0]
```
I hoped, that this way, sensorsim would get two GPUs that can could share the memory, but it actually creates two separate sensorsim containers:
sensorsim-0 which uses GPU 0 and sensorsim_1 which uses GPU 1. 
Is this the desired behavior?

Regarding the cache setting, I'll give it a try and report back

Yeah, we don't support multi-GPU containers at the moment. But each scene is only a couple of GB large, so for NuRec that shouldn't be necessary. 
But the default cache size is 4... which _could_ be just a bit too much for 10GB. 
Please let me know if reducing it works.
This PR updates the NuRec container, you can try it as well: #63

> But the default cache size is 4... which _could_ be just a bit too much for 10GB. Please let me know if reducing it works.

Looking good! With `defines.nre_cache_size:2`.
Running now for 3+ hours without any crash.

Regarding the PR, I will have a look later this week. 

Thank you very much  for the help
Nice, happy it works. Closing the issue but feel free to reopen as needed.
